feed.title: Learning & Roadmaps — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: BTK Akademi
entry.content:
The Turkish ICT Authority’s free online learning platform: programming, cyber security, AI and networking courses, with a certificate on completion. Unlike paid Turkish course marketplaces it is state-run and free; taking a course needs an account.

https://www.btkakademi.gov.tr/

entry.title: Coderspace
entry.content:
A career platform for developers in Turkey: company-sponsored bootcamps and hackathons, plus public interview questions, salary data, roadmaps and a developer glossary. Unlike Techcareer it sells an interactive Python and data course platform (Pro) and publishes salary figures.

https://coderspace.io/

entry.title: How DNS Works
entry.content:
A colourful comic that shows how a DNS query is resolved through resolvers, root and TLD servers. Unlike reference books it makes the process concrete with characters and a short story.

https://howdns.works/

entry.title: How HTTPS Works
entry.content:
A one-page comic that explains HTTPS, certificates and key exchange. Unlike technical specs it conveys the core idea in a few minutes without requiring any cryptography background.

https://howhttps.works/

entry.title: HTTP/2 Explained
entry.content:
A short book by curl's author Daniel Stenberg explaining the HTTP/2 protocol, including headers, streams and server push. More readable than the specification and written from an implementer's view; translated editions exist.

https://github.com/bagder/http2-explained

entry.title: Let's Build a Simple Database
entry.content:
A step-by-step tutorial that builds a SQLite-like database from scratch in C: REPL, B-tree, pager, cursors. Unlike conceptual database explainers, it shows the storage engine internals through working code.

https://cstack.github.io/db_tutorial/

entry.title: Linux Guide and Hints
entry.content:
A community guide to server setup, networking, security and service configuration on the Rocky/RHEL family, step by step. Unlike distro manuals it centres on real deployment scenarios and experienced advice.

https://linuxguideandhints.com/

entry.title: Marko Knoebl: Programming Course Slides
entry.content:
Course slides built from Markdown for React, Vue, Python, data science, HTML/CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript and databases, with exercises and solutions. Unlike video courses these are standalone HTML slides you can download and read offline; CC BY-SA 4.0.

https://marko-knoebl.github.io/slides/

entry.title: SHA-256 Algorithm Visualised
entry.content:
A browser visualisation that animates how SHA-256 turns an input into a hash, showing the bits in memory and each round. Unlike written explanations, you can type your own input and watch every step.

https://sha256algorithm.com/

entry.title: Techcareer.net
entry.content:
A Turkish career platform with company-sponsored bootcamps, job listings and public resources (technical glossary, interview questions, CV samples, university base scores). Unlike Coderspace it has shifted its weight to AI-skills training; the resource pages read without an account.

https://www.techcareer.net/

entry.title: The Illustrated TLS 1.2 Connection
entry.content:
A page that walks through every byte of a TLS 1.2 handshake with colour-coded, annotated and hand-computed values. Unlike most TLS explainers it shows the actual packet contents step by step instead of an abstract diagram.

https://tls12.xargs.org/

entry.title: Web Skills
entry.content:
Lays out the skills to learn as a web developer (HTML, CSS, JS, tooling, testing, performance) as a visual map, with each box linking to a good tutorial. Unlike text-heavy roadmaps it shows the whole field at a glance.

https://andreasbm.github.io/web-skills/

entry.title: What happens when...
entry.content:
A detailed step-by-step account of everything that happens when you type an address in a browser and press Enter (DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP, rendering). It goes deeper than typical 'how the web works' pieces, to the level an interview question wants.

https://github.com/alex/what-happens-when

entry.title: ÖSYM
entry.content:
The body that runs Turkey’s central exams (YKS, KPSS, ALES, YDS); its public pages carry the exam calendar, guides, published question booklets and result statistics. Unlike prep sites it is the official source for dates and rules; applying happens in a separate, authenticated system.

https://www.osym.gov.tr/

entry.title: arxiv-sanity-lite
entry.content:
Karpathy's tool for searching, tagging and recommending arXiv papers; open source.

https://arxiv-sanity-lite.com

entry.title: Awesome Certificates
entry.content:
A list of free computer-science certificates you can add to your résumé. Unlike paid certificate programmes, it picks only free ones.

https://github.com/PanXProject/awesome-certificates

entry.title: Awesome Hackathon
entry.content:
A resource list for running fun and productive hackathons. Unlike participant guides, it focuses on the organiser’s side: planning, judging, tools and platforms.

https://github.com/dribdat/awesome-hackathon

entry.title: Awesome Product Management
entry.content:
A resource list for becoming a better product manager. Unlike general career lists, it gathers books, frameworks and tools specific to product management.

https://github.com/dend/awesome-product-management

entry.title: Awesome Roadmaps
entry.content:
A list gathering clear roadmaps to improve your knowledge across fields.

https://github.com/liuchong/awesome-roadmaps

entry.title: Awesome STEAM
entry.content:
Supplementary learning resources for science, technology, engineering, arts and maths. Unlike general learning lists, it uses the STEAM frame that includes the arts and focuses on school-level extras.

https://github.com/RahulBirCodes/awesome-steam

entry.title: Awesome Workshopper
entry.content:
A list of interactive command-line tutorials (workshoppers). Unlike browser-based tutorials, you solve exercises in the terminal with your own editor — the format NodeSchool uses.

https://github.com/therebelrobot/awesome-workshopper

entry.title: Awesome YouTubers
entry.content:
A list of quality YouTube channels that teach technology. Unlike a YouTube search, it hand-picks channels by topic.

https://github.com/JoseDeFreitas/awesome-youtubers

entry.title: CSS Diner
entry.content:
A game teaching CSS selectors by picking dishes on a table. Unlike dry drills it turns selector syntax into a visual, fun puzzle.

https://flukeout.github.io/

entry.title: Distill
entry.content:
A research journal explaining machine-learning ideas through interactive visuals. Unlike classic paper journals it explains interactively; publication is on hiatus, but the archive remains valuable.

https://distill.pub

entry.title: Duolingo
entry.content:
A platform teaching languages through gamified, short daily lessons. Unlike course-based learning it builds a habit through daily streaks; in exchange, speaking practice is limited.

https://www.duolingo.com

entry.title: Flexbox Defense
entry.content:
A site teaching CSS Flexbox through a tower-defence game. Unlike the docs it fixes each alignment property with a game move.

http://www.flexboxdefense.com/

entry.title: Full Stack Open
entry.content:
The University of Helsinki’s free, end-to-end full-stack course teaching React, Node and GraphQL. Unlike Udemy-style courses, assignments are assessed and it can award university credit (ECTS).

https://fullstackopen.com

entry.title: Learn to Code With Me
entry.content:
A resource gathering paths, tools and career advice for self-taught coders. Unlike single-topic sites it addresses “where to start and how to turn it into a job”.

https://learntocodewith.me/

entry.title: Silent Teacher
entry.content:
A game that teaches the basics of programming by trial and error, with no word of explanation. Unlike a lecture it has you discover the rule yourself.

https://silentteacher.toxicode.fr/

entry.title: SoloLearn
entry.content:
A platform teaching programming on mobile through small lessons and community. Unlike long courses it is bite-sized enough to progress even on the bus.

https://www.sololearn.com/

entry.title: TechGuide
entry.content:
A site giving software’s different career paths (frontend, data, mobile) as visual roadmaps. Unlike a single resource it maps what to learn in which order for a role.

https://techguide.sh/

entry.title: 01 Edu Public
entry.content:
The open course-and-project repository of the 01 Edu school, built on a teacherless, peer-reviewed model. Unlike video courses it is project-based: with deliberately ambiguous tasks it teaches you to build your own solution.

https://github.com/01-edu/public

entry.title: APMG International
entry.content:
An accreditation body running examinations for the AXELOS frameworks and others. Unlike the framework owners it is an independent examination institute — the same ITIL exam is available through several, and APMG is one of them.

https://apmg-international.com/

entry.title: AXELOS
entry.content:
The owner of the ITIL, PRINCE2 and MSP frameworks. Unlike the security bodies it sits on the service and project management side — ITIL is the shared vocabulary of corporate IT, and security teams use the same terms for incident handling.

https://www.axelos.com/

entry.title: BCS
entry.content:
The UK’s chartered professional body for IT, which certifies and also accredits university programmes. Unlike commercial examination institutes it is a professional institution, and a step on the path to chartered engineer status.

https://www.bcs.org/

entry.title: CertNexus
entry.content:
A body issuing vendor-neutral certificates in emerging fields: cybersecurity, data science, AI and IoT. Its difference from the established organisations is that focus — a yardstick in areas the traditional catalogues have not caught up with.

https://certnexus.com/

entry.title: CompTIA
entry.content:
A common entry rung through Security+, Network+ and A+. Unlike senior certifications it demands no prior experience, which is why it appears in first-job listings and in the US defence sector’s DoD 8570 list. Do not expect depth.

https://www.comptia.org/

entry.title: EXIN
entry.content:
A Dutch vendor-neutral examination institute certifying in information security management (ISO 27001) and data protection. Unlike training providers it only examines: where you learned the material is not its concern.

https://www.exin.com/

entry.title: GAQM
entry.content:
A body issuing vendor-neutral certificates across a wide field — project management, quality, security. Against the established organisations it is cheap with flexible entry requirements; in exchange, employer recognition is limited.

https://www.gaqm.org/

entry.title: PECB
entry.content:
A body certifying auditors and implementers against ISO standards including 27001, 22301 and 9001. Against EXIN it operates through an accredited trainer network and confers lead auditor status.

https://pecb.com/
